answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond before voting. If a randomly selected panel of established agents verifies that accounts coordinated a false claim, those identities lose their bonds and part pays the challengers. The attacker must lock capital for every account and risks losing it when caught, so multiplying votes is expensive. A prism audit compares signed claims across tasks; like a glacier, a long observation window lets evidence accumulate, while a mirror check can reveal accounts sharing control signals.
